monthly_review.summary: This month shows reduced volume and slower average pace versus last month, with notable drops in cadence and aerobic TE — consistent with a deliberate recovery or transition phase, not deterioration.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence rebounded sharply from 118 spm in July to 152 spm in August — a 34 spm increase that aligns with faster turnover on recent runs and reflects meaningful neuromuscular re-engagement after the low-cadence July sessions (e.g., 18 spm and 44 spm on 2026-07-31).

goal_tracker.message: You’d need 42.1 km across 6 remaining sessions — averaging 7.0 km/session — to match last month’s volume. However, given persistent sleep debt (13/14 nights <7h) and low training readiness (7-day avg = 47), chasing this number risks undermining aerobic resilience. Focus instead on quality over quantity: maintain current easy-run pacing and cadence gains while protecting sleep.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated running economy
insights.body: Running economy recently spiked to 253.5 ml O2/kg/km (‘Recreational’ rating), up from rolling median 253.5 — but note: 4 of last 6 recorded values are ≥253.5, and all occurred during periods of sub-5h average sleep (recent avg = 4.8h); poor sleep impairs neuromuscular coordination and increases vertical oscillation (recent avg = 7.7 cm), which directly worsens economy.

insights.title: Strong recovery balance masks underlying fatigue accumulation
insights.body: Recovery balance is high (1.81), yet training readiness 7-day avg is only 47 — the lowest in the dataset — and Body Battery is down 8.0% vs baseline (59.0 vs 64.1). This suggests autonomic resilience (HRV) is intact, but subjective and energetic readiness is lagging, likely due to cumulative sleep debt and inconsistent recovery behaviors.

insights.title: Improved aerobic decoupling despite higher zone 3 time
insights.body: This month’s zone 3 % rose to 32% (vs 29% in July), yet latest aerobic decoupling is 4.8% — just under the 5% aerobic threshold — and better than median recent decoupling (7.11%). This signals improved fatigue resistance *within* moderate-intensity efforts, likely supported by lower avg HR (137 vs 141) and improved aerobic TE (2.5 vs 2.9).

insights.title: Cadence recovery coincides with VO2max stabilization and stride normalization
insights.body: Cadence jumped from 118 spm (July) to 152 spm (August), matching improved stride length stability (recent stride range: 66.6–83.6 cm) and reduced ground contact time (298–307 ms vs July’s 370 ms). VO2max held steady at 39–40, suggesting neuromuscular efficiency gains are supporting aerobic capacity without additional cardiovascular stress.
